question: want to pick and carry with the rough terrain across the yard. is that allowed, who has to be in charge of it, and anything about the tires?
gold_answer: Traveling with a load is prohibited if the manufacturer prohibits it. Otherwise, a competent person must supervise. That person decides whether rated capacity needs to be reduced and makes the calls on load position, boom location, ground support, travel route, overhead obstructions and speed, and those decisions must be carried out. On equipment with tires, the manufacturer's specified tire pressure must be maintained.

key_quote.text: For equipment with tires, tire pressure specified by the manufacturer is maintained.

question: we're doing a bunch of repetitive heavy picks all near max line pull, do i have to do the brake check every single one
gold_answer: No. The brakes must be tested by lifting the load a few inches and applying the brakes whenever a load is 90% or more of the maximum line pull. In duty cycle or repetitive lifts where every lift is 90% or more, the test is required only on the first lift, not on the ones after it.

key_quote.text: The operator must test the brakes each time a load that is 90% or more of the maximum line pull is handled

question: found something on the crane that needs fixd, is it enuf to just tell the next shift guy verbaly?
gold_answer: No. The operator must promptly report it in writing to the person the employer designated to receive such information and, where there are successive shifts, to the next operator. The employer must notify all affected employees at the beginning of each shift about the needed adjustments or repairs and any alternative measures.

key_quote.text: The operator must, in writing, promptly inform the person designated by the employer to receive such information

question: I can see the hook fine from the cab but once the load swings behind the building I lose it where it sets down. Do I gotta have a signal guy for that or can I just go slow?
gold_answer: Yes. You must have a signal person whenever the point of operation (the load travel or the area near or at load placement) is not in full view of the operator. Going slow doesn't replace that.

key_quote.text: The point of operation, meaning the load travel or the area near or at load placement, is not in full view of the operator.

question: walking the crawler across the laydown yard and the counterweight blocks my view going backwards do i need a spotter signal person for travel or only for picks
gold_answer: A signal person is required when the equipment is traveling and the view in the direction of travel is obstructed. This covers travel too, not just lifting.

key_quote.text: When the equipment is traveling, the view in the direction of travel is obstructed.

question: Two questions on radios. Can we just run the crane signals on the same channel the electricians and the GC use? And do we have to check the radios out before starting, or is it fine as long as they worked yesterday?
gold_answer: No. Signals have to go over a dedicated channel. The only exceptions are cranes/signal persons sharing a channel to coordinate crane operations, and crane work on or next to railroad tracks. The devices also have to be tested on site before operations begin to make sure transmission is effective, clear, and reliable.

key_quote.text: The device(s) used to transmit signals must be tested on site before beginning operations to ensure that the signal transmission is effective, clear, and reliable.

question: We're running a locomotive crane on the rail spur and the operator has to coordinate with train moves on the next track over. Does the signal radio still need its own dedicated channel, or can it be on the railroad channel?
gold_answer: There's an exception to the dedicated-channel rule when a crane works on or next to railroad tracks and the operator's actions have to be coordinated with other equipment or trains on the same or adjacent tracks. So a shared channel is allowed in that case.

key_quote.text: Where a crane is being operated on or adjacent to railroad tracks, and the actions of the crane operator need to be coordinated with the movement of other equipment or trains on the same or adjacent tracks.

expert_review.why: The text doesn't say how far the shared-channel allowance goes, for example whether it can be the railroad's own operations channel.

question: is it ok if the operater just holds the walkie in his hand and keys it while he runs the levers
gold_answer: No. The operator has to receive signals through a hands-free system.

key_quote.text: The operator's reception of signals must be by a hands-free system.

question: For voice signals over the radio, what's the right order to say things? And if we swap in a new signal guy after lunch, do we have to go over the voice signals again?
gold_answer: Every voice signal gives the function (hoist, boom, etc.), then the direction, then distance and/or speed, then the function and stop command. The operator, signal person, and lift director (if there is one) only have to meet again if a worker is added or substituted, there's confusion, or a signal is changed. A new signal person counts as a substitution, so yes, you go over them again.

key_quote.text: function (such as hoist, boom, etc.), direction; distance and/or speed; function, stop command.

question: radio cut out mid pick and I got nothing but static what am I supposed to do keep going on the last call or what
gold_answer: If signal communication is interrupted, the operator must safely stop the operations that need signals. Don't resume until communication is back and a proper signal has been given and understood. Don't keep going on the last signal.

key_quote.text: the operator must safely stop operations requiring signals until it is reestablished and a proper signal is given and understood.

question: We've got two tower cranes with overlapping swing and one signal person talking to both on a single shared channel. Is that legal, and how does she keep the operators from both reacting to the same call?
gold_answer: Yes. Multiple cranes and one or more signal persons may share a dedicated channel to coordinate operations. When a signal person talks to more than one crane, she must name the crane before giving each function/direction, or use an equally effective way of identifying which crane the signal is for.

key_quote.text: for each signal, prior to giving the function/direction, the signal person must identify the crane/derrick the signal is for

question: Under what circumstances may non-standard hand signals be used in lieu of the Standard Method, and what must occur before they are used?
gold_answer: Non-standard hand signals are allowed only when the Standard Method is infeasible, or when an operation or attachment isn't covered by the Standard Method. Before the operation, the signal person, operator, and lift director (if there is one) must contact each other and agree on the non-standard signals.

key_quote.text: the signal person, operator, and lift director (where there is one) must contact each other prior to the operation and agree on the non-standard hand signals that will be used.

question: so like who's allowed to signal me? only one guy? what if some laborer sees a problem, and when the signal guy says swing left is that his left or mine
gold_answer: Only one person may give signals to a crane at a time. The exception is that anyone who becomes aware of a safety problem must give the stop or emergency stop signal. All directions from the signal person must be given from the operator's direction perspective, so 'left' means your left.

key_quote.text: All directions given to the operator by the signal person must be given from the operator's direction perspective.

question: where does the hand signal chart have to be for a guy derrick job, on the derrick itself?
gold_answer: The hand signal chart has to be posted either on the equipment or conspicuously in the vicinity of the hoisting operations. It doesn't have to be on the derrick itself.

key_quote.text: Hand signal charts must be either posted on the equipment or conspicuously posted in the vicinity of the hoisting operations.

question: Our company wants to use a light-panel/tablet system instead of hand or voice signals. What does the employer have to show to be allowed to do that, and does the transmission method have to fit the site?
gold_answer: New signals (other than hand, voice, or audible) are allowed only if the employer shows they give at least equally effective communication as voice, audible, or Standard Method hand signals, or that they follow a national consensus standard that does. The signals and how they're sent (line of sight, video, radio, etc.) must also be appropriate for the site conditions.

key_quote.text: The new signals provide at least equally effective communication as voice, audible, or Standard Method hand signals

expert_review.why: The text doesn't say what counts as 'demonstrating' equal effectiveness for a specific system.

question: guys walking out on the stick to do some work, at what height do they gotta tie off? we're not putting the crane together or taking it apart, just normal work
gold_answer: For non-assembly/disassembly work, while just walking point-to-point, fall protection is required with an unprotected side or edge more than 6 ft above a lower level on non-lattice booms and non-horizontal lattice booms, but on horizontal lattice booms only where the fall distance is 15 ft or more. At a work station on any part of the equipment, including any type of boom, it is required above 6 ft. The work-station rule excepts employees at or near the draw-works while the equipment is running, in the cab, or on the deck.

key_quote.text: with an unprotected side or edge more than 6 feet above a lower level

question: What is the fall protection trigger height for employees doing assembly or disassembly work on a crane, and are there any locations on the machine where it does not apply?
gold_answer: During assembly/disassembly, fall protection is required when an employee is on a walking/working surface with an unprotected side or edge more than 15 feet above a lower level. It does not apply when the employee is at or near the draw-works while the equipment is running, in the cab, or on the deck.

key_quote.text: unprotected side or edge more than 15 feet above a lower level, except when the employee is at or near draw-works

question: lattice boom is layed down flat on blocking and a guy needs to walk from one end to the other, fall is maybe 10 ft. does he need fall protection just walking it
gold_answer: On a horizontal lattice boom, fall protection for moving point-to-point is required only when the fall distance is 15 feet or more, so a 10-foot fall does not trigger it while he is just walking. If he stops to work at a work station on the boom, fall protection is required above 6 feet. Non-lattice booms, and lattice booms that are not horizontal, need fall protection above 6 feet even when just moving point-to-point. All of this applies to non-assembly/disassembly work.

key_quote.text: On horizontal lattice booms where the fall distance is 15 feet or more.

expert_review.why: The answer assumes non-assembly/disassembly work. Whether he is 'moving' or 'at a work station' is a call made in the field.

question: on a tower crane do the tie off heights change when we're jumping/climbing the mast vs regular operations?
gold_answer: Yes. For erecting, climbing and dismantling a tower crane, fall protection is required above 15 feet. For other work it is required above 6 feet, except at or near the draw-works while the equipment is running, in the cab, or on the deck.

key_quote.text: For erecting, climbing, and dismantling work, the employer must provide and ensure the use of fall protection equipment for employees who are on a walking/working surface with an unprotected side or edge more than 15 feet

question: Two questions about boom walkways: which lattice booms are required to have them and how wide do they have to be? And can we put handrails on them, and if so how tall can they be?
gold_answer: Lattice-boom equipment manufactured after November 8, 2011 must have boom walkways if the boom's vertical profile (chord centerline to chord centerline) is 6 feet or more. The walkways must be at least 12 inches wide. Guardrails are not required. They are prohibited if pendant ropes or bars could snag them, or if they are the removable type. Where they are allowed, they can be no more than 45 inches high.

key_quote.text: must be equipped with walkways on the boom(s) if the vertical profile of the boom (from cord centerline to cord centerline) is 6 or more feet

question: can the ironworker clip his lanyard to the crane hook instead of finding a beam what has to happen for that to be ok
gold_answer: A personal fall arrest system may be anchored to the hook or load line only if all three conditions are met. First, a qualified person has determined that the set-up and rated capacity (including the hook, load line and rigging) meet or exceed the 1926.502(d)(15) criteria. Second, the operator is at the work site and has been told the crane is being used this way. Third, no load is suspended from the load line.

key_quote.text: No load is suspended from the load line when the personal fall arrest system is anchored to the crane/derrick's hook (or other part of the load line).

question: new tower crane going up, what does the access between the ground, cab, machinery deck and mast have to have? any standards it has to meet
gold_answer: Tower cranes manufactured after November 8, 2011 must have safe access and egress between the ground and the cab, machinery platforms and tower (mast), using devices such as steps, handholds, ladders and guardrails/railings/grabrails. These devices must meet ISO 11660-1:2008(E) and ISO 11660-3:2008(E), or SAE J185 (May 2003), except where infeasible. Walking/stepping surfaces must be slip-resistant.

key_quote.text: must meet the criteria of ISO 11660-1:2008(E) (incorporated by reference, see § 1926.6) and ISO 11660-3:2008(E) (incorporated by reference, see § 1926.6) or SAE J185 (May 2003)

question: do we hav to barricade the swing radius on the cherry picker? site is real tight no room for cones or tape whats the alternitive
gold_answer: Yes. Where the rotating superstructure creates a struck-by or pinch/crush hazard in accessible areas, the employer must put up and maintain control lines, warning lines, railings or similar barriers to mark the hazard area. If the employer can show that barriers are not feasible either on the ground or on the equipment, the area must instead be clearly marked with warning signs (such as 'Danger—Swing/Crush Zone') plus high-visibility markings on the equipment. Employees must be trained on what those markings mean.

key_quote.text: Erect and maintain control lines, warning lines, railings or similar barriers to mark the boundaries of the hazard areas.

expert_review.why: Whether barriers are truly infeasible on both the ground and the equipment is a judgment the employer has to demonstrate.

question: I'm the operator and I saw the oiler duck in behind the counterweight where I can't see him. Then I get a signal to swing. Can I swing?
gold_answer: No. If the operator knows an employee went into the swing/crush hazard area, the operator must not rotate the superstructure until told, through a pre-arranged system of communication, that the employee is in a safe position. Before going out of the operator's view, the employee (or someone he instructs) must make sure the operator is informed.

key_quote.text: the operator must not rotate the superstructure until the operator is informed in accordance with a pre-arranged system of communication that the employee is in a safe position

question: we're setting wood trusses and the guys are under the load hooking up. do we need latched hooks or can we use J hooks, and who has to rig it
gold_answer: When employees are in the fall zone hooking, unhooking or guiding a load, or making the initial connection, all of the following apply. The load must be rigged to prevent unintentional displacement. Hooks with self-closing latches (or equivalent) must be used, but J hooks are allowed for setting wooden trusses. The materials must be rigged by a qualified rigger.

key_quote.text: Exception: “J” hooks are permitted to be used for setting wooden trusses.

question: tilting up concrete wall panels, who is allowed to be near the panel while it's being raised? can anyone stand under it?
gold_answer: During a tilt-up or tilt-down, no employee may be directly under the load. Only employees essential to the operation may be in the fall zone: those physically guiding the load, closely monitoring and giving instructions on its movement, or attaching/detaching it, and only where the employer can show it is infeasible to do that from outside the fall zone. Boom free fall is prohibited with anyone in the fall zone, and load line free fall is prohibited with anyone directly under the load.

key_quote.text: No employee must be directly under the load.

expert_review.why: Whether working from outside the fall zone is 'infeasible' depends on the employer's showing and site conditions.

question: We run a live boom crane on a barge. Today the load is going over a cofferdam and there's a crew working in the fall zone. Is free fall of the boom allowed?
gold_answer: No. A floating crane, or a land crane on a barge, is one of the cases where a live boom is allowed, but only when none of the prohibited circumstances are present. A load over a cofferdam with employees in the fall zone of the boom or load is prohibited, so boom free fall can't be used.

key_quote.text: The load is over a cofferdam, except where there are no employees in the fall zone of the boom or the load.

question: lowering a load down an empty shaft with no one in it, can i free fall the load line? and is it different for the boom
gold_answer: No. Load line free fall is prohibited whenever the load is over a shaft, with no exception for an empty shaft, so controlled load lowering is required. For a live boom, the shaft prohibition does not apply when no employees are in the shaft. Even then, a live boom is allowed only if no other prohibited circumstance is present and the equipment was made before October 31, 1984, or is a floating crane or a land crane on a vessel.

key_quote.text: The load is over a shaft, except where there are no employees in the shaft.

question: got a trainee in the seat today, can he make the pick if the 13.8kv lines are like 15 ft from where the boom could swing out to max radius?
gold_answer: No. Unless certified, an operator-in-training may not operate if any part of the equipment, load line or load could get within 20 feet of a line up to 350 kV (50 feet if over 350 kV) when operated out to maximum working radius in the work zone. A 13.8 kV line 15 feet away is inside that 20-foot zone.

key_quote.text: could get within 20 feet of a power line that is up to 350 kV, or within 50 feet of a power line that is over 350 kV

question: how long can the trainer step away from the operator in training and how often
gold_answer: The trainer must monitor the operator-in-training at all times except for short breaks. A break can last no more than 15 minutes, with no more than one break per hour. Right before the break the trainer must tell the trainee what specific tasks to do and what limits to follow, and those tasks must be within the trainee's abilities.

key_quote.text: The break lasts no longer than 15 minutes and there is no more than one break per hour.

question: Trainee is up in the tower crane cab and I'm on the ground, so I can't actually see him. Is that ok or do I have to be able to see him like on a mobile?
gold_answer: For tower cranes, the trainer and operator-in-training only have to be in direct communication with each other; line of sight isn't required. For equipment other than tower cranes, they must be in direct line of sight and communicate verbally or by hand signals.

key_quote.text: For tower cranes: The operator's trainer and the operator-in-training must be in direct communication with each other.

question: Does a derrick operator need a CCO type certification under 1926.1427 or is that only for cranes
gold_answer: Operators of derricks don't have to comply with § 1926.1427, so they don't need its certification. The training requirements in the derrick section (§ 1926.1436) still apply.

key_quote.text: Operators of derricks (see § 1926.1436), sideboom cranes (see § 1926.1440), or equipment with a maximum manufacturer-rated hoisting/lifting capacity of 2,000 pounds or less

question: our litle picker is only rated 2000 lbs max, do my guys need to be certfied to run it or no training at all??
gold_answer: Operators of equipment with a maximum manufacturer-rated capacity of 2,000 pounds or less are exempt from the § 1926.1427 certification/evaluation requirements. The training requirements in § 1926.1441 still apply, so they still need training.

key_quote.text: equipment with a maximum manufacturer-rated hoisting/lifting capacity of 2,000 pounds or less (see § 1926.1441) are not required to comply with § 1926.1427

question: boss says I gotta pay for my own crane card out of pocket, is that legit
gold_answer: No. When operator certification or licensure is required, the employer must provide it at no cost to the employee.

key_quote.text: the employer must provide the certification/licensure at no cost to employees.

question: If I switch companies does my certification come with me? What if it was my old company's in-house audited program instead of an accredited testing outfit? And how long is each one good for?
gold_answer: A certification from an accredited crane operator testing organization is portable among employers who must use that option and is valid for 5 years. A certification from an employer's audited program isn't portable; it only counts while you work for (and operate for) the employer that issued it. It is also valid for 5 years.

key_quote.text: A certification issued under this option is portable among employers who are required to have operators certified under this option.

question: For purposes of compliance with 1926.1427, what is the maximum period a state- or locally-issued crane operator license may be considered valid?
gold_answer: The license is valid for the period stipulated by the licensing department/office, but no longer than 5 years.

key_quote.text: a license is valid for the period of time stipulated by the licensing department/office, but no longer than 5 years.

question: we're starting our own in house operator cert program. when does the first audit have to happen, how often after that, and if the auditor finds a big problem what happens
gold_answer: The program must be audited within 3 months of starting and at least every 3 years after that. If the auditor finds a significant deficiency, no operator can be qualified until the auditor confirms it's corrected, and the program must be audited again within 180 days of that confirmation. The auditor must also file a documented report with the appropriate OSHA Regional Office within 15 days of determining there is a deficiency.

key_quote.text: The employer program must be audited within 3 months of the beginning of the program and at least every 3 years thereafter.

question: what goes on the operator evaluation paperwork
gold_answer: The document must give the operator's name, the evaluator's name and signature, the date, and the make, model and configuration of the equipment used, and it must be available at the worksite while the operator works for that employer. For operators assessed under paragraph (f)(2), it must instead reflect the date of the employer's determination of the operator's abilities and the make, model and configuration of equipment on which the operator previously demonstrated competency.

key_quote.text: The operator's name; the evaluator's name and signature; the date; and the make, model, and configuration of equipment used in the evaluation.

question: New hire showed up with a current accredited certification for lattice crawlers. Can I just put him on our crawler with the luffing jib tomorrow since he's certified?
gold_answer: No. A certificate alone doesn't make him qualified. The employer must also evaluate him to confirm he has the skills, knowledge and ability to recognize and avert risk for that equipment, including its size and configuration (e.g., luffing jib, counterweight setup), and document the evaluation. The evaluator must be an employee or agent of the employer.

key_quote.text: Possession of a certificate or degree cannot, by itself, cause a person to be qualified for purposes of paragraph (f)(1).

expert_review.why: Whether prior evaluations can carry over (f)(2) or whether the equipment is 'substantially different' under (f)(5) depends on the employer's facts.

question: my last company qualified me as a signal person through their own evaluator, does the new outfit have to accept that
gold_answer: No. A signal person assessment by an employer's own qualified evaluator (Option 2) is not portable, so other employers can't use it. The new employer has to qualify you again, either with its own qualified evaluator or with documentation from a third-party qualified evaluator.

key_quote.text: An assessment by an employer's qualified evaluator under this option is not portable—other employers are not permitted to use it to meet the requirements of this section.

question: how does a signal man actually prove hes qualified, like what testing, and does his paper need to say radio vs hand signals
gold_answer: The signal person must pass an oral or written test and a practical test showing they know and are competent in the signals used (the Standard Method if hand signals are used), have a basic understanding of equipment operation and crane dynamics, and know §§ 1926.1419–1422 and 1926.1428. Yes, the documentation must specify each type of signaling (e.g., hand, radio) they're qualified for, and it must be available at the site.

key_quote.text: through an oral or written test, and through a practical test.

question: Operator took his cert test in Spanish. Our rental crane's manual and load chart are English only. Can he run it?
gold_answer: No. A test can be given in any language the candidate understands, and the certification must note that language. But the operator may only run equipment whose required materials, such as operations manuals and load charts, are written in the language of the certification, so here that means Spanish.

key_quote.text: The operator is only permitted to operate equipment that is furnished with materials required by this subpart, such as operations manuals and load charts, that are written in the language of the certification.

question: our mechanic wants to run the crane around the yard to check out a hydraulic fix he did. hes not certified. is that ok or does a certified op have to be in the seat
gold_answer: Yes, within limits. Maintenance, inspection and repair personnel may operate the equipment only for functions needed to do maintenance, inspect it, or verify its performance. They must also either work under the direct supervision of an operator who meets §1926.1427, or be familiar with the operation, limitations, characteristics and hazards of that type of equipment.

key_quote.text: The operation is limited to those functions necessary to perform maintenance, inspect the equipment, or verify its performance.

question: Does the guy doing repairs on the crane have to be some kind of 'qualified' person, or can any shop hand do it?
gold_answer: Maintenance and repair personnel must meet the definition of a qualified person for the equipment and for the specific maintenance or repair tasks they perform.

key_quote.text: Maintenance and repair personnel must meet the definition of a qualified person with respect to the equipment and maintenance/repair tasks performed.

question: my company says i gotta pay for the crane training they're making me take. can they do that??
gold_answer: No. Whenever Subpart CC requires training, the employer must provide it at no cost to the employee.

key_quote.text: Whenever training is required under subpart CC, the employer must provide the training at no cost to the employee.

question: Old friction machine, boom's been laid down on the boom rest. What are operators supposed to be trained to do before picking it up off the support? And what if it was a hydraulic rig instead and the brake slips?
gold_answer: On friction equipment, operators must be trained to first raise the boom a short distance, enough to take the boom's load, to see whether the boom hoist brake needs adjusting. The same practice applies to other equipment with a boom, but those machines usually have no way to adjust the brake, so if the brake does not hold, the machine needs repair.

key_quote.text: first raise the boom a short distance (sufficient to take the load of the boom) to determine if the boom hoist brake needs to be adjusted

expert_review.why: The rule says 'friction equipment', which can include truck-mounted friction cranes as well as crawlers, so the equipment tag is an assumption.

question: do maintanence guys who start up the crane need tagout trainng or is that just for operaters
gold_answer: Both need it. The employer must train each operator, and each other employee allowed to start or energize the equipment or run its controls (such as maintenance and repair employees), in the tag-out and start-up procedures of §1926.1417(f) and (g).

key_quote.text: each additional employee authorized to start/energize equipment or operate equipment controls (such as maintenance and repair employees), in the tag-out and start-up procedures

question: A rigger finished training last year, but the foreman has since watched him repeatedly stand in the swing radius. Is the employer obligated to do anything training-wise, and does the employer have to check that people actually understood the training in the first place?
gold_answer: Yes on both counts. The employer must evaluate every employee trained under Subpart CC to confirm they understood the training. The employer must also give refresher training in the relevant topics when the employee's conduct or an evaluation of their knowledge shows retraining is needed.

key_quote.text: when, based on the conduct of the employee or an evaluation of the employee's knowledge, there is an indication that retraining is necessary

question: is the hydraulic cylinder thing where the boom drifts when it cools off actually on the written cert test for hydro cranes
gold_answer: Yes. Appendix C's general technical knowledge criteria include the effects of thermal expansion and contraction in hydraulic cylinders, as well as the basics of hydraulic and other machine power flow systems.

key_quote.text: The effects of thermal expansion and contraction in hydraulic cylinders.

question: We run a crane on a barge. Does the written operator exam criteria in Appendix C say anything specific about working on water?
gold_answer: Yes. Appendix C says candidates should know that operations on water require specific procedures and skill levels. It also lists knowing safe procedures for lifting loads from beneath the surface of the water.

question: what electrical protection stuff do they test you on for the written? like grounding, insulated links, what else
gold_answer: Appendix C covers the technical limitations of these protections against electrical hazards: grounding, proximity warning devices, insulated links, boom cages, and proximity to electric power lines, radii, and microwave structures.

question: site's tight and we cant get the outriggers out all the way on the RT. what should the operator know per the written exam stuff for that, and how does the load chart play in
gold_answer: Appendix C expects operators to know safe procedures for using less than full outrigger/crawler or stabilizer extensions, and how to check that there is room to extend outriggers and counterweights. On load charts, they must know how to match the chart to the crane's setup, including whether outriggers/stabilizers are extended or retracted, and make sure the chart is the right one for that configuration.

key_quote.text: How to relate the chart to the configuration of the crane, crawlers, or outriggers/stabilizers extended or retracted, jib erected or offset, and various counterweight configurations.

expert_review.why: Appendix C only lists exam knowledge areas; the actual capacity rules for reduced outrigger extension depend on the manufacturer's charts and on other sections.

question: super wants us to just fly the guys up in a man basket instead of building scaffold cuz it's faster. is that allowed?
gold_answer: Not just because it's faster. Hoisting employees with the crane is prohibited unless the employer shows that putting up, using and taking down conventional access (personnel hoist, ladder, stairs, aerial lift, elevating work platform, scaffold) would be more hazardous, or isn't possible because of the structural design or worksite conditions. This doesn't apply to steel erection work under subpart R or to routine underground shaft access under 1926.800.

key_quote.text: would be more hazardous, or is not possible because of the project's structural design or worksite conditions

question: how levle does the crane have to be b4 we do a personel lift
gold_answer: It must be uniformly level, within 1 percent of level grade. It must also sit on footing that a qualified person has found firm and stable enough.

key_quote.text: uniformly level, within one percent of level grade

question: truck crane man basket job one side is tight can we short jack the outriggers on that side if the chart allows it
gold_answer: No. For hoisting personnel, all outriggers and stabilizers must be extended and locked, every one extended the same amount, following the manufacturer's procedures and load charts.

key_quote.text: The amount of extension must be the same for all outriggers and stabilizers

question: For a suspended personnel platform, what is the capacity limit, and what has to be counted in the load?
gold_answer: The total load must not exceed 50 percent of the rated capacity for the radius and configuration. The total includes the loaded platform, the hook, the load line and the rigging. Proof testing is the only exception.

key_quote.text: must not exceed 50 percent of the rated capacity for the radius and configuration of the equipment, except during proof testing

question: knuckle boom with a basket — do I need a boom angle indicator and boom hoist limiter like the big cranes or is there something different
gold_answer: Articulating cranes are exempt from the variable-angle-boom requirement for a boom angle indicator and a boom hoist limiting device. Instead, they must have a properly functioning automatic overload protection device.

key_quote.text: Articulating cranes must be equipped with a properly functioning automatic overload protection device.

question: How often do we have to do the trial lift with the basket? Every day? And if we move the crane to the other side of the building and come back, do we redo it? What if we change the route?
gold_answer: A trial lift is required right before each shift in which personnel will be hoisted. It must be repeated whenever the equipment is moved and set up in a new location or returned to a previously used one. It must also be repeated when the lift route changes, unless the competent person determines the new route brings no new safety factors.

key_quote.text: The trial lift must be performed immediately prior to each shift in which personnel will be hoisted.

question: proof test on the man basket how much weight how long do we hang it and can we do it at the same time as the trial lift
gold_answer: At each jobsite before hoisting employees, and after any repair or modification, the platform and rigging must be proof tested to 125 percent of the platform's rated capacity. The test load must be evenly distributed, lowered by controlled load lowering, braked, and held suspended for at least 5 minutes. The proof test may be done at the same time as the trial lift.

key_quote.text: the platform and rigging must be proof tested to 125 percent of the platform's rated capacity

question: We held the pre-lift meeting Monday with the operator, signal guy, the two ironworkers going up and the foreman. Tuesday a third worker gets added to the basket crew at the same location. Do we need another meeting?
gold_answer: Yes. The pre-lift meeting must be repeated for any employee newly assigned to the operation. It must also be held before the trial lift at each new work location. Attendees are the operator, the signal person (if used), the employees being hoisted, and the person responsible for the task.

key_quote.text: must be repeated for any employees newly assigned to the operation

question: gusting 25 up at the basket but steady wind is like 12. do we automatically shut down the man lift?
gold_answer: Not automatically. When wind, sustained or gusts, exceeds 20 mph at the personnel platform, a qualified person must decide whether it is unsafe to lift personnel. If it is unsafe, the lift must not start, or must be stopped if already underway. Gusts count, so 25 mph gusts trigger that review.

question: We need to put two guys in a basket about 40 feet from a 500 kV transmission line. We're a general contractor, not a utility. Can we do it?
gold_answer: No, not unless the work itself is covered by subpart V (Power Transmission and Distribution); being a general contractor rather than a utility does not by itself decide that. Otherwise, hoisting personnel within 50 feet of a line over 350 kV is prohibited (the limit is 20 feet for lines up to 350 kV), so 40 feet from a 500 kV line is not allowed.

key_quote.text: hoisting personnel within 50 feet of a power line that is over 350 kV, is prohibited

question: can a derrick travel w/ people in the platform if we go real slow
gold_answer: No. Derricks are prohibited from traveling while personnel are being hoisted, however slow the travel.

key_quote.text: Derricks are prohibited from traveling while personnel are hoisted.

question: rough terrain crane with guys in the basket, can we creep it down the slab to the next bay instead of landing them and resetting? there's honestly no better way
gold_answer: Traveling while hoisting employees is prohibited except on fixed rails, or where the employer shows there is no less hazardous way, but that exception does not apply to rubber-tired equipment like an RT. Even when travel is allowed, it must be on a fixed track or designated runway, limited to boom length, with the boom parallel to travel and a full trial run first.

key_quote.text: This exception does not apply to rubber-tired equipment.

question: Our shop is building a personnel platform. What enclosure is required below the midrail, and can the gate swing out?
gold_answer: From the toeboard to at least the mid-rail, the platform must be enclosed with solid material or expanded metal with openings no larger than 1/2 inch, plus a subpart M guardrail system. Gates must not swing outward unless the platform is so small (for example, 1-person) that an inward swing with safe entry isn't feasible. Gates must also have a device that prevents accidental opening.

key_quote.text: expanded metal having openings no greater than 1/2 inch (1.27 cm)

question: hoisting a guy on the pile driving rig, no anti two block on it. telescopic crane. what do we do instead
gold_answer: Anti two-block isn't required when hoisting personnel in pile driving. On a telescopic boom crane you must do both: clearly mark the cable where the operator can easily see it, at a point that gives enough time to stop the hoist, and use a spotter in direct communication with the operator. On a lattice boom crane, either one is enough.

key_quote.text: For telescopic boom cranes: Clearly mark the cable (so that it can be easily seen by the operator) at a point that will give the operator sufficient time to stop the hoist to prevent two-blocking, and use a spotter

question: factory boom mounted basket has its own little winch. can the guys in the basket pick stuff with it while they're up there
gold_answer: Yes, but only with a factory-produced boom-mounted platform that has the winch as original equipment. The load on the winch line must not exceed 500 pounds or the rated capacity of the winch and platform. Otherwise, no lifts may be made on other load lines while personnel are hoisted, except in pile driving.

key_quote.text: only where the load on the winch line does not exceed 500 pounds and does not exceed the rated capacity of the winch and platform

question: doing a tandem pick w two cranes on a bridge beam tmrw, who's supposed to put the lift plan together? can the super just wing it
gold_answer: No. A lift where more than one crane supports the load has to be planned before it starts, and a qualified person must develop the plan. If that qualified person decides engineering expertise is needed, the employer must provide it.

question: who runs a two crane lift does it have to be a competent person or qualified person or both and do they have to go over the plan with the crew
gold_answer: The lift director must be either one person who meets the criteria for both a competent person and a qualified person, or a competent person assisted by one or more qualified persons. The lift director must review the plan in a meeting with all workers who will be involved in the operation.

question: we sent the manufactuer our plans for a modifcation to the crane and they never wrote back. how long do we hafta wait b4 we can go another route
gold_answer: If the manufacturer got a detailed description and doesn't acknowledge the request or start the review within 30 days (or declines to review it), the employer can go ahead only if a registered professional engineer who is a qualified person for that equipment approves the change, says which configurations the approval covers, and updates the load charts, procedures, manuals and plates/tags/decals. The original safety factor must not be reduced.

key_quote.text: fails, within 30 days, to acknowledge the request or initiate the review

question: The manufacturer said they'd look at our proposed boom modification and started reviewing it, but it's been about four months with no decision. Can we have our own PE sign off on it now?
gold_answer: Yes. If the manufacturer agreed to review the proposal but hasn't finished within 120 days of getting the detailed description, a registered professional engineer who is a qualified person for that equipment can approve it, specify the configurations it applies to, and update the load charts, procedures, manuals and decals. The original safety factor must not be reduced.

key_quote.text: fails to complete the review of the proposal within 120 days of the date it was provided the detailed description of the proposed modification/addition

question: OEM looked at our request to add a counterweight package and said no. One time they gave us a letter with their engineering reasons, another time they just said no over the phone. Can we still do the mod in either case?
gold_answer: If the manufacturer reviews the technical safety merits, rejects the proposal, and explains why in writing, the modification is prohibited. If it rejects the proposal without giving written reasons, the employer may treat that as a refusal to review and use the registered PE route, as long as the original safety factor is not reduced.

key_quote.text: If the manufacturer rejects the proposal but does not explain the reasons for the rejection in writing, the employer may treat this as a manufacturer refusal to review the request

expert_review.why: Whether a verbal 'no' counts as a rejection without written reasons is an interpretation call.

question: how much weight is the cab roof supposed to hold if guys stand up there
gold_answer: Any part of the cab roof that serves as a workstation for rigging, maintenance or other equipment-related tasks must be able to support 250 pounds without permanent distortion.

key_quote.text: must be capable of supporting 250 pounds without permanent distortion

question: rigger wants to zip tie the safety latch back on the hook so the choker comes off easier, is that legal
gold_answer: Not just to make unhooking easier. Under 1926.1433(d)(4), a latch may be removed, disabled or tied back only if a qualified person determines it is safer to hoist and place the load that way, and routes are pre-planned so only workers needed for hooking or unhooking are in the fall zone. However, under 1926.1425(c)(2), when workers are in the fall zone hooking, unhooking, guiding or making the initial connection, hooks with self-closing latches or their equivalent must be used (except J-hooks for setting wooden trusses).

expert_review.why: independent check: The gold answer omits 1926.1425(c)(2): workers hooking, unhooking or guiding in the fall zone must use self-closing latches or their equivalent (J-hook exception for wood trusses). This limits the 1433(d)(4)(ii) exception in the unhooking scenario asked about.

question: What prototype testing standard applies to a tower crane manufactured after November 2010?
gold_answer: Tower cranes manufactured on or after November 8, 2010 must meet the prototype testing requirements in BS EN 14439:2006.

key_quote.text: Tower cranes manufactured on or after November 8, 2010 must meet the prototype testing requirements in BS EN 14439:2006

question: got an older crawler built like 2005, what design standard does it have to meet, the new ASME one or what
gold_answer: Crawler, truck and locomotive cranes built before November 8, 2010 can meet any of these: the applicable design, construction and testing requirements of ANSI B30.5-1968, PCSA Std. No. 2 (1968), the ASME B30.5-2004 portions listed in paragraph (b), or the applicable DIN standards in effect when the crane was made.

key_quote.text: Crawler, truck and locomotive cranes manufactured prior to November 8, 2010 must meet the applicable requirements for design, construction, and testing

question: Our barge crane was put together from a base from one company and a boom from another. We want to modify it. Is there a way to do that without manufacturer approval?
gold_answer: Yes. If the equipment is designed for marine work sites and has major structural components from more than one manufacturer, a registered professional engineer who is a qualified person for that equipment can approve the modification, specify the configurations it covers, and update the load charts, manuals and decals. The original safety factor must not be reduced.

key_quote.text: The equipment is designed for marine work sites, contains major structural components from more than one manufacturer

expert_review.why: Whether a given barge setup counts as 'designed for marine work sites' with 'major structural components' from several makers is a judgment call.

question: For a hydraulic boom truck crane built in 2015: (1) what prototype test options are there, and (2) can computer modeling replace the physical testing?
gold_answer: (1) Option A: run all tests in SAE J1063 (Nov. 1993) Table 1 and meet the strength margins in Table 2. Option B: meet BS EN 13000:2004, with computer modeling showing all SAE J1063 load cases meet the Table 2 margins. (2) Under Option B the physical SAE testing is still required, unless the modeling's reliability has been shown by a documented history of verification through strain gauge measuring (alone or combined with other physical testing).

key_quote.text: unless the reliability of the analysis methodology (computer modeling) has been demonstrated by a documented history of verification through strain gauge measuring

question: how plumb does the tower gotta be if the manufacturer doesnt give a tolerance
gold_answer: The tower must be erected plumb to the manufacturer's tolerance, and a qualified person must verify it. If the manufacturer gives no tolerance, the tower must be plumb to at least 1:500, which is about 1 inch in 40 feet.

key_quote.text: the crane tower must be plumb to a tolerance of at least 1:500 (approximately 1 inch in 40 feet)

question: Anti two-block quit on our tower crane mid shift. Can we keep picking, and how long do we have to get it fixed?
gold_answer: The operator must safely stop until a temporary measure is in place. The measure is either marking the hoist cable where the operator can see it, at a point that leaves time to stop before two-blocking, or using a spotter in direct communication with the operator. As a Category I aid, it must be repaired within 7 calendar days. If parts are documented as ordered within 7 days, the deadline is 7 calendar days after the parts arrive.

key_quote.text: must be repaired no later than 7 calendar days after the deficiency occurs

question: Wind gauge on the tower crane is dead. 1) where's it supposed to be mounted, 2) what do we use meanwhile, 3) how many days to fix it?
gold_answer: On tower cranes the wind speed indicator must be mounted above the upper rotating structure. On self-erectors it goes at or above jib level. In the meantime you can use wind speed from a working indicator on another tower crane on the same site, or have a qualified person estimate it. As a Category II aid, it must be repaired within 30 calendar days. If parts were documented as ordered within 7 days but arrive too late, the repair is due 7 days after receipt.

key_quote.text: must be repaired no later than 30 calendar days after the deficiency occurs

question: trolly limit switch not working on the hammerhead, whats the work around
gold_answer: There are two temporary options. Option A: mark the trolley rope where the operator can see it, at a point that leaves enough time to stop before the end stops. Option B: use a spotter in direct communication with the operator whenever work is within 10 feet of the outer or inner trolley end stops.

key_quote.text: A spotter who is in direct communication with the operator must be used when operations are conducted within 10 feet of the outer or inner trolley end stops.

question: If the trolley brake on a tower crane stops working, can we use a spotter or some other workaround and keep running?
gold_answer: No. The trolley brake is a required safety device. The operator must safely stop, the crane must be taken out of service, and work can't resume until the brake works properly again. Alternative measures are not permitted.

key_quote.text: Alternative measures are not permitted to be used.

question: What are the load test requirements following the erection of a tower crane, and whose procedure governs the test?
gold_answer: A load test must be done after each erection, using certified weights or weights scaled on a certified scale with a current calibration certificate. Follow the manufacturer's instructions when they exist. Otherwise, use written load test procedures developed by a registered professional engineer familiar with that type of equipment.

key_quote.text: A load test using certified weights, or scaled weights using a certified scale with a current certificate of calibration, must be conducted after each erection.

question: Our tower crane is tied into the building. On the monthly, which bolts and tie-in stuff do we check, and what's added at the annual?
gold_answer: Because the crane is tied in, the monthly covers mast and structural bolts above the upper-most brace support, checked for loose or dislodged condition. It also covers the upper-most tie-in, braces, floor supports and floor wedges, checked for loose or dislodged parts. The annual adds a check of all turntable and tower bolts for proper condition and torque.

key_quote.text: all turntable and tower bolts must be inspected for proper condition and torque

question: how many guy lines does a guy derrick need
gold_answer: At least 6, equally spaced. A qualified person or the derrick manufacturer can approve a different arrangement, but only if they revise the rated capacity to make up for it.

key_quote.text: The minimum number of guys must be 6, with equal spacing

question: We just reinstalled a stiffleg derrick. What test load do we use before first use, what if our biggest pick is heavier than that, and what paperwork do we keep and for how long?
gold_answer: A competent person must load test it at 100% to 110% of rated capacity, unless the manufacturer or a qualified person recommends otherwise. The test load can never be less than the maximum anticipated load. The test record must show the date, the results and the tester's name. Keep it until the derrick is re-tested or dismantled, whichever comes first.

key_quote.text: Test loads must be at least 100% and no more than 110% of the rated capacity

question: does the guy running the derrick need a crane operator card
gold_answer: No. The operator qualification and certification rule (1926.1427) does not apply to derricks. The employer must still train each derrick operator on safe operation of the equipment they will run.

key_quote.text: Section 1926.1427 of this subpart (Operator qualification and certification) does not apply.

question: derrick gonna sit idle about six weeks what do we do with the boom
gold_answer: If it will be out of service 30 days or more, secure the boom one of these ways: lay it down; sling the load block to a stationary member as nearly under the head as possible; on a guy derrick, raise it vertical and secure it to the mast; or on a stiffleg derrick, secure it against the stiffleg.

question: new base mounted hoist for the derick, what % do we load test it to and do we have to if the manufaturer already did
gold_answer: New hoists must be load tested to at least 110% and no more than 125% of rated capacity, unless the manufacturer recommends otherwise. If the manufacturer already did that testing, the requirement is met.

key_quote.text: new hoists are load tested to a minimum of 110% of rated capacity, but not more than 125% of rated capacity

question: What extra stuff gets checked on a derrick beyond the normal crane inspections, daily and yearly?
gold_answer: Daily: check the guys for proper tension. Annually: check the gudgeon pin for cracks, wear and distortion, and check the foundation supports for continued ability to carry the imposed loads.

key_quote.text: Daily: Guys for proper tension.

question: we got a 30 ton crane bolted permanent on a barge, its built for marine use not a derrick. how much list can we run before we're out of bounds
gold_answer: For equipment built for marine use by permanent attachment (not a derrick) and rated over 25 tons, the maximum allowable list is 7 degrees and the maximum allowable trim is 7 degrees. At 25 tons or less the limit is 5 degrees each.

question: Putting our crawler on a deck barge for a bridge job. Manufacturer says it can take 3 degrees out of level. Whats the max list/trim allowed on the barge?
gold_answer: For a land crane on a barge, the barge's maximum allowable list and trim can't exceed the smallest of 5 degrees, the crane manufacturer's figure, or the qualified person's figure if the manufacturer gives none. Here that means 3 degrees. The limit must also keep all deck surfaces above water and the whole bottom submerged.

key_quote.text: does not exceed the least of the following: 5 degrees, the amount specified by the crane/derrick manufacturer

question: Two divers going down off the barge using the crane to lower them. Can we use the crane for other picks while they're down there? And does the operator gotta stay in the seat the whole time?
gold_answer: No. A crane used to get divers into and out of the water can't be used for anything else until all the divers are back on board. Yes, the operator has to stay at the controls at all times. Signals between the operator and the tender need either a clear line of sight or electronic transmission.

key_quote.text: When used for more than one diver, it must not be used for any other purpose until all divers are back on board.

question: do i need an anti two block on the floatin crane if were just setting sheet pile no people on the hook
gold_answer: On floating cranes/derricks and land cranes on barges, an anti two-block device is required only when hoisting personnel or hoisting over an occupied cofferdam or shaft. Setting sheet pile with nobody on the hook and no occupied cofferdam or shaft below doesn't require one under this section.

key_quote.text: An anti two-block device is required only when hoisting personnel or hoisting over an occupied cofferdam or shaft.

question: Who is permitted to perform the four-year internal inspection of a crane barge, and how long must that inspection record be retained?
gold_answer: A marine engineer, marine architect, licensed surveyor, or other qualified person with expertise in vessels/flotation devices must survey the internal portion. The documentation must be kept for at least 4 years and made available to everyone who does inspections.

key_quote.text: except that the documentation for that inspection must be retained for a minimum of 4 years

question: our barge is a jack up legs are down on the river bottom holding the whole thing up do the barge crane rules still apply
gold_answer: No. The floating crane/barge section (1926.1437) doesn't apply to jacked barges when the jacks are deployed to the river, lake, or sea bed and the barge is fully supported by the jacks.

question: we're doing construction work inside a plant and using the building's bridge crane. do we follow the construction crane rules or what?
gold_answer: An overhead or gantry crane permanently installed in a facility and used in construction is covered by 29 CFR 1910.179, except 1910.179(b)(1). The Subpart CC requirements don't apply to it.

key_quote.text: The requirements of § 1910.179, except for § 1910.179(b)(1), and not the requirements of this subpart CC, apply

question: Got a launching gantry for setting bridge girders, built in 2015, moves on its own wheels, not permanent. Which rules cover it, and does 1910.179(b)(2) apply?
gold_answer: Non-permanent gantries like this fall under listed Subpart CC sections (1926.1400–1414, 1417–1425, 1426(d), 1427–1434, 1437, 1439, 1441), listed portions of 1910.179, and specified ASME B30.2-2005 sections because it was built on or after Sept 19, 2001. 1910.179(b)(2) applies only to equipment made before Sept 19, 2001, so it doesn't apply here.

question: does a dedicated pile driver need anti two blok and a load weighing devise? ours is a 2009 rig
gold_answer: The anti two-block device requirement (1926.1416(d)(3)) doesn't apply to dedicated pile drivers. The load weighing device requirement (1926.1416(e)(4)) applies only to dedicated pile drivers manufactured after November 8, 2011, so a 2009 rig doesn't need one.

question: pipeline crew here, do our sideboom cat operators need the NCCCO cert like crane guys, and is the old live boom sideboom still legal
gold_answer: Sideboom cranes are exempt from 1926.1427 (operator qualification and certification). question: Can I put a guy in a basket on our little 1 ton capacity boom truck to get him up to the roof
gold_answer: No. Equipment with a rated hoisting/lifting capacity of 2,000 pounds or less must not be used to hoist personnel.

question: small 2000 lb rated crane bought new last year doesnt have an anti two block switch is that ok
gold_answer: Equipment rated 2,000 lbs or less and made more than one year after November 8, 2010 needs one of two things. question: We want to run a small rough terrain crane around on the deck of the derrick barge without chaining it down or corralling it. Is that allowed, what do we need, and what happens if the seas pick up past the plan limits?
gold_answer: Yes, for a mobile auxiliary crane on a floating crane's deck, if a marine engineer or a registered PE familiar with floating crane design writes and signs a plan. question: how tight can the bridge run to the building steel? whats the minimum gap overhead and off to the sides on an overhead crane
gold_answer: At least 3 inches of clearance overhead and 2 inches laterally must be provided and maintained between the crane and obstructions.
