question: Two things on the bridge footwalk: how much headroom do I need above it, and what load does the walkway itself have to hold?
gold_answer: Where footwalks are provided there must be at least 48 inches of headroom. Footwalks must be rigid and designed for a distributed load of at least 50 pounds per square foot, with an antislip walking surface (wood qualifies).

key_quote.text: in no case shall less than 48 inches of headroom be provided

question: wats the biggest gap u can have to step acros getting from the ladder onto the bridge walkway
gold_answer: Access to the cab or bridge walkway must be by a conveniently placed fixed ladder, stairs or platform that requires no step over a gap greater than 12 inches (30 cm). Fixed ladders must meet subpart D.

key_quote.text: requiring no step over any gap exceeding 12 inches (30 cm)

question: how tall does the end stop on the trolley rail have to be if the wheel hits it right on the tread
gold_answer: A trolley stop that engages the wheel tread must be at least as high as the radius of the wheel. Stops are required at the trolley's travel limits and must be fastened to resist the forces of contact.

key_quote.text: A stop engaging the tread of the wheel shall be of a height at least equal to the radius of the wheel.

question: We're spec'ing the hoist holding brake. The hoist uses dynamic braking for lowering control. What percent of full-load hoisting torque does the brake need, and does that change if we go with a mechanical load brake or put two holding brakes on?
gold_answer: With control braking other than mechanical (like dynamic), the holding brake must be at least 125% of full-load hoisting torque at the point where it's applied. With mechanical control braking it's 100%, and if two holding brakes are used, each must be at least 100%.

key_quote.text: 125 percent when used with a control braking means other than mechanical

question: ladle crane in the melt shop with power control braking, is one holding brake on the hoist enough?
gold_answer: No. Every independent hoisting unit on a crane handling hot metal that has power control braking must have at least two holding brakes.

key_quote.text: Each independent hoisting unit of a crane handling hot metal and having power control braking means shall be equipped with at least two holding brakes.

question: is there a voltage limit on the pendant
gold_answer: Yes. Voltage at pendant push-buttons can't exceed 150 volts AC or 300 volts DC. The control circuit overall is capped at 600 volts AC or DC.

key_quote.text: The voltage at pendant push-buttons shall not exceed 150 volts for a.c. and 300 volts for d.c.

question: Our shop has a pendant-controlled bridge crane. Maintenance wants to know where the main disconnect from the runway conductors has to be mounted, and what ways the operator on the floor is allowed to kill power from down there.
gold_answer: An enclosed switch or circuit breaker that can be locked open must be in the leads from the runway conductors, mounted on the bridge or footwalk near the runway collectors. The floor disconnect must be one of three types: a nonconductive rope attached to the main disconnect, an undervoltage trip on the main breaker operated by an emergency stop button in the pendant, or a main line contactor operated by a switch or pushbutton in the pendant.

key_quote.text: This disconnect shall be mounted on the bridge or footwalk near the runway collectors.

question: how many wraps gotta stay on the drum with the hook all the way down
gold_answer: At least two wraps of rope must stay on the drum when the hook is at its lowest position. The rope end must be anchored with a clamp securely attached to the drum, or with a socket arrangement approved by the crane or rope manufacturer.

key_quote.text: No less than two wraps of rope shall remain on the drum when the hook is in its extreme low position.

question: just reroped the hoist w/ U-bolt clips, which side does the saddle go and do i need to go back and retorque them
gold_answer: The U-bolts go on the dead (short) end of the rope, and clip spacing and number follow the clip manufacturer's recommendations. After a newly installed rope has run for one hour, all the clip bolt nuts must be retightened.

key_quote.text: When a newly installed rope has been in operation for an hour, all nuts on the clip bolts shall be retightened.

question: Under 1910.179, which overhead cranes need an audible warning device such as a gong, and are any types exempt?
gold_answer: Every crane with a power traveling mechanism needs a gong or other effective warning signal. Floor-operated cranes are exempt.

key_quote.text: Except for floor-operated cranes a gong or other effective warning signal shall be provided for each crane equipped with a power traveling mechanism.

question: we got a big storage bridge outside in the yard, what do we need for wind? and the rail clamps grab the rail head, anything special about that
gold_answer: Outdoor storage bridges need automatic rail clamps and a wind-indicating device that gives the bridge operator a visible or audible alarm at a predetermined wind speed. If the clamps act on the rail heads, any beads or weld flash on the rail heads must be ground off.

key_quote.text: If the clamps act on the rail heads, any beads or weld flash on the rail heads shall be ground off.

question: Cab-on-bridge crane, bridge full-load speed is 200 fpm. How far does the bridge brake have to stop it in at full speed and full load? And what's the max pedal force if it's a foot brake?
gold_answer: The brake must stop the bridge within a distance in feet equal to 10% of full-load speed in fpm, so 20 feet at 200 fpm when traveling at full speed with full load. A foot-operated brake must not need more than 70 pounds of applied force to develop the manufacturer's rated brake torque.

key_quote.text: within a distance in feet equal to 10 percent of full load speed in feet per minute when traveling at full speed with full load

question: what has to go on the monthly hook inspection paperwork for our bridge crane? is a visual every day enough or do we need the record too
gold_answer: Hooks get a visual check for deformation or cracks every day, and a monthly inspection that is documented. The monthly record must include the inspection date, the signature of the person who did it, and the hook's serial number or other identifier.

key_quote.text: monthly inspection with a certification record which includes the date of inspection, the signature of the person who performed the inspection and the serial number, or other identifier, of the hook inspected

question: Hook on the gantry looks opened up and a little twisted. At what point do I have to scrap it, and can the shop just weld it and heat it back into shape?
gold_answer: Discard the hook if it has cracks, a throat opening more than 15 percent over normal, or more than 10° of twist from the plane of the unbent hook. Repairing it by welding or reshaping is not generally recommended. If someone does it anyway, it must be done under competent supervision, and the hook must pass a load test (no more than 125% of rated load unless the manufacturer recommends otherwise) before it goes back in use.

key_quote.text: more than 15 percent in excess of normal throat opening or more than 10° twist from the plane of the unbent hook

expert_review.why: The rule discourages weld/reshape repairs without banning them; whether to allow a repair is a judgment call for competent supervision.

question: Crane in bay 3 sat parked for about 3 months while the line was down. What inspection does it need before we put it back to work? What if it had been 8 months?
gold_answer: Idle 1 month or more but less than 6 months: do the frequent inspection items in (j)(2) plus the idle-rope inspection in (m)(2) before returning it to service. Idle more than 6 months: do a complete inspection covering both (j)(2) and (j)(3), plus (m)(2), before returning it to service.

key_quote.text: idle for a period of 1 month or more, but less than 6 months

expert_review.why: The text doesn't say which rule applies to a crane idle exactly 6 months.

question: how often do standby cranes have to be inspectd
gold_answer: Standby cranes must be inspected at least semi-annually. The inspection covers the frequent inspection items in (j)(2) and the rope inspection in (m)(2).

key_quote.text: Standby cranes shall be inspected at least semi-annually

question: How often does the wire rope on an overhead crane need a thorough inspection, and what records are required?
gold_answer: All running ropes need a thorough inspection at least once a month. Keep a certification record on file where appointed personnel can readily get to it. It must show the date, the inspector's signature, and an identifier for the ropes inspected.

key_quote.text: A thorough inspection of all ropes shall be made at least once a month

question: rope on the hoist hasnt moved in like 6 weeks cause the crane was shut down, who has to sign off before we use it again
gold_answer: Rope that has sat idle for a month or more because of a shutdown or storage needs a thorough inspection for all types of deterioration before use. An appointed person must do the inspection, and their approval is required before the rope is used again. A certification record with the date, signature and rope identifier must be available.

key_quote.text: shall be performed by an appointed person whose approval shall be required for further use of the rope

question: we just rebuilt the trolley on our bridge crane. how heavy can the load test go, and what about setting the upper limit switch?
gold_answer: Test loads can be no more than 125 percent of rated load unless the manufacturer recommends otherwise, and the test reports must be kept on file for appointed personnel. Set the hoist limit switch trip point by testing with an empty hook at increasing speeds up to maximum speed. The switch must trip in time to keep the hook or block from contacting any part of the trolley.

key_quote.text: Test loads shall not be more than 125 percent of the rated load unless otherwise recommended by the manufacturer.

question: Gotta work on the brakes on one of two bridge cranes sharing a runway. What do I need to do before I start wrenching on it?
gold_answer: Before work starts: move the crane to where it interferes least with other cranes and operations, put all controllers in the off position, and open the main or emergency switch and lock it open. Put warning or "out of order" signs on the crane and on the floor beneath it or on the hook, where they can be seen from the floor. Because another crane runs on the same runway, use rail stops or another suitable means to keep it from hitting the idle crane.

key_quote.text: The main or emergency switch shall be open and locked in the open position.

question: how far down can i lower the hook before im out of rope on the drum
gold_answer: Never lower the load to the point where fewer than two full wraps of rope remain on the hoisting drum.

key_quote.text: The load shall not be lowered below the point where less than two full wraps of rope remain on the hoisting drum.

question: start of shift do i have to check the upper limit on the hoist and can i just run it into the limit to stop it every pick
gold_answer: Yes. At the start of each operator's shift, test the upper limit switch of each hoist with no load, either inching the block into the limit or running it in at slow speed. If the switch doesn't work right, notify the appointed person immediately. The upper hoist limit switch must never be used as an operating control.

key_quote.text: The hoist limit switch which controls the upper limit of travel of the load block shall never be used as an operating control.

question: Picking something close to the crane's capacity — is there a brake check I'm supposed to do first?
gold_answer: Yes. Each time a load close to rated load is handled, the operator must test the brakes by raising the load a few inches and applying them.

key_quote.text: The brakes shall be tested by raising the load a few inches and applying the brakes.

question: can we drag a skid sideways across the floor with the gantry hook instead of getting under it
gold_answer: Not as a general rule. Side pulls are prohibited unless a responsible person specifically authorizes them after determining that the crane's stability won't be endangered and its parts won't be overstressed.

key_quote.text: Cranes shall not be used for side pulls except when specifically authorized by a responsible person

expert_review.why: Deciding whether a side pull keeps the crane stable and avoids overstress is an engineering judgment the text doesn't define.

question: whats the diffrence between frequent and periodic inspecton and what extra stuff gets looked at on the periodic
gold_answer: Frequent inspections happen at daily to monthly intervals, and periodic inspections at 1 to 12-month intervals, depending on activity, severity of service and environment. A periodic inspection includes all the frequent items plus: deformed, cracked or corroded members; loose bolts or rivets; cracked or worn sheaves and drums; worn parts such as pins, bearings, shafts and gears; brake wear; accuracy of load and wind indicators; powerplants; chain drive sprockets and chain stretch; and pitting or deterioration of electrical contactors, limit switches and pushbutton stations.

key_quote.text: (a) Frequent inspection—Daily to monthly intervals. (b) Periodic inspection—1 to 12-month intervals.

question: Guy wants to wrap the hoist rope around a pipe bundle and hook it back to itself to save time, then ride the load over to the other bay. Any of that okay?
gold_answer: No to both. The hoist rope or chain must not be wrapped around the load; attach the load to the hook with slings or other approved devices. Also, no hoisting, lowering or traveling is allowed while any employee is on the load or hook.

key_quote.text: While any employee is on the load or hook, there shall be no hoisting, lowering, or traveling.

question: whats the max load rating as a percent of tipping for a crawler with no outriggers vs with outriggers fully out
gold_answer: For a crawler crane without outriggers, load ratings can't exceed 75% of the tipping load. With outriggers fully extended, the limit is 85%.

key_quote.text: Crawler, without outriggers | 75 ; Crawler, using outriggers fully extended | 85

question: For rating a locomotive crane, when is it considered to be tipping, and how level does the track have to be?
gold_answer: A locomotive crane counts as tipping, with or without outriggers, when half of the wheels farthest from the load leave the rail. For rating purposes the crane must stand on track that is level within 1 percent grade.

key_quote.text: Tipping with or without the use of outriggers occurs when half of the wheels farthest from the load leave the rail.

question: hook on our plant's truck crane looks kinda opened up and a lil twisted, at what point is it junk?
gold_answer: Under the frequent inspection items for crawler, locomotive and truck cranes, a hook is deficient if it has cracks, a throat opening more than 15 percent over normal, or more than 10° of twist from the plane of the unbent hook. Such a hook is a deficiency to be found in inspection and corrected before the crane is used.

key_quote.text: more than 15 percent in excess of normal throat opening or more than 10° twist from the plane of the unbent hook

expert_review.why: 1910.180(d)(3)(v) lists the limits as inspection items but does not itself say 'discard'; whether such a hook is junk is field practice.

question: Our truck crane at the plant (general industry, not construction) sat in the yard about 3 months with the ropes still reeved. What inspections do we have to do before we put it back to work, and does anybody have to sign off on the rope?
gold_answer: A crane idle for 1 month or more but less than 6 months needs a frequent-type inspection under (d)(3) plus the idle-rope inspection under (g)(2)(ii) before going back in service. The rope must get a thorough inspection for all types of deterioration by an appointed or authorized person, whose approval is required for further use. A certification record with the date, the inspector's signature and a rope identifier must be kept readily available.

key_quote.text: A crane which has been idle for a period of one month or more, but less than 6 months, shall be given an inspection conforming with requirements of paragraph (d)(3)

question: how ofen do standby cranes need inspectd
gold_answer: Standby cranes must be inspected at least semiannually, under the frequent-inspection items in (d)(3) and the idle-rope inspection in (g)(2)(ii). Standby cranes exposed to adverse environments should be inspected more often.

key_quote.text: Standby cranes shall be inspected at least semiannually

question: After we fixed the boom we want to do a load test. How heavy can the test load go, and do we need paperwork?
gold_answer: Test loads may not exceed 110% of the rated load at any selected working radius. Written reports must be available showing the test procedures and confirming that the repairs or alterations are adequate.

key_quote.text: Test loads shall not exceed 110 percent of the rated load at any selected working radius.

question: can we rerate our plant's truck crane higher than the original chart
gold_answer: Only if the crane manufacturer or final assembler approves the rating change. Rerating tests follow SAE J765 for crawler, truck and wheel-mounted cranes, or paragraphs (c)(1)(i) and (ii) for locomotive cranes, and the rerating test report must be readily available.

key_quote.text: No cranes shall be rerated in excess of the original load ratings unless such rating changes are approved by the crane manufacturer or final assembler.

question: pick is in the structural part of the chart not stability how close do i gotta know the weight
gold_answer: When a load is limited by structural competence rather than stability, its weight must be determined within plus or minus 10% before it is lifted.

key_quote.text: it shall be ascertained that the weight of the load has been determined within plus or minus 10 percent before it is lifted

question: How many wraps have to stay on the drum when I'm booming down or lowering into a deep hole?
gold_answer: Neither the load nor the boom may be lowered past the point where fewer than two full wraps of rope remain on their drums.

key_quote.text: Neither the load nor the boom shall be lowered below the point where less than two full wraps of rope remain on their respective drums.

question: truck crane - ok to swing the load around over the front of the truck?
gold_answer: No. On truck-mounted cranes, loads may not be lifted over the front area unless the crane manufacturer approves it.

key_quote.text: On truck-mounted cranes, no loads shall be lifted over the front area except as approved by the crane manufacturer.

question: On the locomotive crane, can I count on the rail clamps to keep it from tipping? And if I'm not using outriggers, is there anything I have to do with the truck springs?
gold_answer: No. Rail clamps may not be used to restrain a locomotive crane from tipping. Before lifting without outriggers, you must apply some means to keep the load from being carried by the truck springs.

key_quote.text: Rail clamps shall not be used as a means of restraining tipping of a locomotive crane.

question: we dropped the counterweight off our plant's truck crane to move it around the yard, can we still make a few small picks w/o it
gold_answer: Generally a crane can't be operated without the full ballast or counterweight the maker specifies. The exception is a truck crane that has dropped its ballast or counterweight: it may be operated temporarily, with special care, and only for light loads. The manufacturer's specified counterweight must never be exceeded.

key_quote.text: truck cranes that have dropped the ballast or counterweight may be operated temporarily with special care and only for light loads without full ballast or counterweight in place

expert_review.why: The rule does not define 'light loads' or 'temporarily', so applying it takes judgment and the manufacturer's guidance.

question: working near hot lines with a crawler at the plant, what does 1910.180 say about clearance
gold_answer: Section 1910.180 sets no clearance distances of its own. For operations near overhead electric lines it refers to § 1910.333(c)(3).

key_quote.text: For operations near overhead electric lines, see § 1910.333(c)(3).

expert_review.why: The actual clearance distances are in 1910.333(c)(3), which is not in the provided text.

question: For a crawler, locomotive or truck crane in general industry, what are the requirements for the monthly running rope inspection, including who may perform it and what must be documented?
gold_answer: Under 1910.180(g)(1), all ropes in use must be thoroughly inspected at least monthly by an appointed or authorized person. Any deterioration causing appreciable loss of strength must be carefully observed, and it must be determined whether further use would be a safety hazard. A certification record with the inspection date, the inspector's signature and a rope identifier must be kept on file where readily available.

key_quote.text: A thorough inspection of all ropes in use shall be made at least once a month

question: moving the crane down the road to the next job what do i need to do with the boom the upper and the hook
gold_answer: In transit, carry the boom in line with the direction of motion. Secure the superstructure against rotation, except when negotiating turns with an operator in the cab or with the boom supported on a dolly. Lash or restrain the empty hook so it can't swing freely.

key_quote.text: The superstructure shall be secured against rotation, except when negotiating turns when there is an operator in the cab or the boom is supported on a dolly.

question: how many busted wires before i gotta toss a wire rope choker? found a few snapped ones in one lay
gold_answer: Take a wire rope sling out of service right away if one rope lay has 10 broken wires scattered randomly, or 5 broken wires in one strand within one rope lay.

key_quote.text: Ten randomly distributed broken wires in one rope lay, or five broken wires in one strand in one rope lay.

question: Two questions on our chain slings: how often do they need the full thorough inspection, not the daily one, and what records do we have to keep?
gold_answer: Alloy steel chain slings need a thorough periodic inspection by a designated competent person. How often depends on use, service conditions, type of lifts and experience, but it can never be more than 12 months apart. The employer must keep a record of the most recent month each sling was thoroughly inspected and make it available for examination.

key_quote.text: Such inspections shall in no event be at intervals greater than once every 12 months.

question: chain sling got left next to the heat treat oven might have gone over a thousand degrees can we still use it if it looks ok
gold_answer: If the alloy steel chain sling was heated above 1000°F, it must be permanently removed from service, even if it looks fine. When service temperatures exceed 600°F, the maximum working load limit must be reduced following the chain or sling manufacturer's recommendations.

key_quote.text: Employers must permanently remove an alloy steel-chain slings from service if it is heated above 1000 degrees F.

question: I've got a 1/2 inch alloy chain sling, and at the worst link the calipers read 3/8 inch (24/64). Is it still good, or does it come out of service?
gold_answer: It comes out of service. Table N-184-1 sets a minimum allowable size of 25/64 inch at any point of the link for 1/2-inch chain, and 24/64 inch is below that. Chain worn under the table minimum at any point must be removed from service.

key_quote.text: If the chain size at any point of the link is less than that stated in Table N-184-1, the employer must remove the chain from service.

question: how far can a sling hook be opend up or twistd befor its scrap
gold_answer: Remove the sling from service if the hook has opened more than 15 percent of its normal throat opening (measured at the narrowest point) or is twisted more than 10 degrees from the plane of the unbent hook. Cracked hooks on chain slings also mean removal.

key_quote.text: Hooks that have been opened more than 15 percent of the normal throat opening measured at the narrowest point or twisted more than 10 degrees from the plane of the unbent hook.

question: We rigged a fiber core wire rope sling to pull hot castings, and it probably got to about 250°F. What happens to the sling? Would an IWRC sling be treated differently?
gold_answer: A fiber core wire rope sling of any grade exposed to more than 200°F must be permanently removed from service. Non-fiber core (for example IWRC) wire rope slings used above 400°F or below -60°F must follow the sling manufacturer's recommendations for that temperature.

key_quote.text: Fiber core wire rope slings of all grades shall be permanently removed from service if they are exposed to temperatures in excess of 200 °F.

question: We're lifting tanks in the pickling area, where there's acid mist. Can we use nylon straps there? If not, would polyester be OK? And does it matter that the straps have aluminum fittings?
gold_answer: Nylon web slings can't be used where acid or phenolic fumes, vapors, sprays, mists or liquids are present. Polyester and polypropylene are barred only around caustics, not acids, so the text doesn't prohibit them in acid mist. Web slings with aluminum fittings are barred only around caustics.

key_quote.text: Nylon web slings shall not be used where fumes, vapors, sprays, mists or liquids of acids or phenolics are present.

expert_review.why: The polyester-in-acid answer rests on the rule being silent about acids. Whether a given chemical counts as an acid or a caustic, and what the manufacturer's chemical-compatibility guidance says, is field judgment.

question: What are the requirements before a repaired synthetic web sling may be returned to service?
gold_answer: The repair must be done by a sling manufacturer or an equivalent entity. The repaired sling must then be proof tested by the manufacturer or equivalent entity to twice its rated capacity before going back into service, and the employer must keep the proof-test certificate. Slings repaired in a temporary manner must not be used.

key_quote.text: Each repaired sling shall be proof tested by the manufacturer or equivalent entity to twice the rated capacity prior to its return to service.

question: can a fiber rope sling get fixed and reused
gold_answer: No. Only natural or synthetic fiber rope slings made from new rope may be used, and repaired or reconditioned fiber rope slings are prohibited. A sling with abnormal wear, broken or cut fibers, rot or similar damage must be removed from service immediately.

key_quote.text: Use of repaired or reconditioned fiber rope slings is prohibited.

expert_review.why: The question is vague: 'rope sling' could mean wire rope. The answer assumes fiber rope, since the text has no general repair ban for wire rope slings.

question: splicing an eye in poly rope for a sling, how many tucks min? and is it the same count for manila?
gold_answer: An eye splice in synthetic fiber rope needs at least 4 full tucks, and in manila at least 3. Short splices need at least 8 full tucks for synthetic (4 each side of center) and 6 for manila (3 each side).

key_quote.text: In synthetic fiber rope, eye splices shall consist of at least four full tucks

question: How much reduction in wire diameter requires a metal mesh sling to be taken out of service?
gold_answer: A metal mesh sling must be removed from service immediately if wire diameter is reduced by 25 percent from abrasion or by 15 percent from corrosion.

key_quote.text: Reduction in wire diameter of 25 per cent due to abrasion or 15 per cent due to corrosion.

question: what temp range is ok for the pvc coated mesh slings versus the bare ones we use on the hot parts
gold_answer: Metal mesh slings impregnated with PVC or neoprene may be used only from 0°F to 200°F. Uncoated metal mesh slings may be used from -20°F to 550°F without reducing the working load limit. Outside those ranges, follow the manufacturer's recommendations.

key_quote.text: Metal mesh slings impregnated with polyvinyl chloride or neoprene may be used only in a temperature range from zero degrees to plus 200 °F.

question: who has to check the slings and how ofen, every shift or what
gold_answer: Each day before use, a competent person designated by the employer must inspect the sling and all its fastenings and attachments for damage or defects. Extra inspections are needed during use where service conditions warrant, and damaged or defective slings must be removed from service immediately.

key_quote.text: Each day before being used, the sling and all fastenings and attachments shall be inspected for damage or defects by a competent person designated by the employer.

question: Can I just tie a knot in the chain to shorten it up, or bolt a link through to hold it? And if a link breaks, can we patch it with a quick link?
gold_answer: No. Slings can't be shortened with knots, bolts or other makeshift devices, and makeshift links or fasteners made from bolts or rods are prohibited on chain slings. Broken lengths of chain can't be repaired with mechanical coupling links or low carbon steel repair links.

key_quote.text: Slings shall not be shortened with knots or bolts or other makeshift devices.

question: tag's gone off one of our chain slings, is that a big deal
gold_answer: Yes. Slings without affixed, legible identification markings must not be used. Alloy steel chain slings must carry permanently affixed, durable identification stating size, grade, rated capacity and reach.

key_quote.text: Alloy steel chain slings shall have permanently affixed durable identification stating size, grade, rated capacity, and reach.

question: crane on a barge, do we actually need a wind gauge out there
gold_answer: Only if wind matters. A competent person must decide whether wind is a factor that needs to be considered. If it is, a wind speed and direction indicator must be used.

key_quote.text: if wind needs to be considered, a wind speed and direction indicator must be used.

question: What wind-related protective equipment is required on an outdoor storage bridge under the general industry overhead and gantry crane standard?
gold_answer: Outdoor storage bridges must have automatic rail clamps and a wind-indicating device that gives the bridge operator a visible or audible alarm at a preset wind velocity. If the clamps act on the rail heads, any beads or weld flash on the rail heads must be ground off.

key_quote.text: A wind-indicating device shall be provided which will give a visible or audible alarm to the bridge operator at a predetermined wind velocity.

question: tandem pick with two cranes next week, who's gotta write up the plan
gold_answer: Any lift where more than one crane or derrick supports the load must be planned before it starts. A qualified person must develop the plan, and it must be designed to ensure the Subpart CC requirements are met.

key_quote.text: The plan must be developed by a qualified person.

question: does a dual crane lift always need an engineer to sign off on it
gold_answer: Not automatically. The plan is developed by a qualified person. Only if that qualified person decides engineering expertise is needed must the employer provide it.

key_quote.text: Where the qualified person determines that engineering expertise is needed for the planning, the employer must ensure that it is provided.

question: Our super is a competent person but not a qualified person. Can he still be the one directing a two-crane lift?
gold_answer: Yes, but only if one or more qualified persons assist him. Otherwise the lift must be directed by someone who meets the criteria for both a competent person and a qualified person.

key_quote.text: directed by a person who meets the criteria for both a competent person and a qualified person, or by a competent person who is assisted by one or more qualified persons

question: do we got to have a meeting before the multi crane lift and who all has to be in it
gold_answer: Yes. The lift director must go over the plan in a meeting with every worker who will be involved in the operation.

key_quote.text: The lift director must review the plan in a meeting with all workers who will be involved with the operation.

question: wheres the load chart and operators manual supposed to be kept, can it stay in the office trailer
gold_answer: No. The load charts (rated capacities), recommended operating speeds, special hazard warnings, instructions and operator's manual must be readily available in the cab at all times for the operator to use.

key_quote.text: must be readily available in the cab at all times for use by the operator.

question: nobody knows what this thing weighs, no paperwork. can i just start picking it and see what the LMI says? whats the cutoff
gold_answer: Yes. You can start hoisting and use a load weighing device, LMI, RCI or RCL to check whether the load exceeds 75% of the maximum rated capacity at the longest radius used in the lift. If the operator asks for that weight information, it must be provided before the lift.

key_quote.text: if it exceeds 75 percent of the maximum rated capacity at the longest radius that will be used during the lift operation

question: does the chart in the cab have to show diffrent capacities for outriggers out vs not, and does it gotta tell me the weakest direction
gold_answer: Yes to both. The cab rating information must include alternate ratings for use and non-use of option equipment that affects capacity, such as outriggers, stabilizers and extra counterweights. It must also include cautions or warnings on limitations, including the least stable direction.

key_quote.text: Alternate ratings for use and nonuse of option equipment which affects rated capacities, such as outriggers, stabilizers, and extra counterweights.

question: I'm the operator and I think the pad is too soft to set up on. What happens next, who has to fix the ground, and what if there's no controlling entity on this job?
gold_answer: If the operator or A/D director finds the ground doesn't meet the requirements, that person's employer must discuss the needed ground preparations with the controlling entity. If there's no controlling entity, the employer with authority at the site to make or arrange ground preparations must provide them.

key_quote.text: that person's employer must have a discussion with the controlling entity regarding the ground preparations that are needed

question: whats the torque spec on the swing bearing bolts for a grove rt9130e? retorquing after the bearing swap
gold_answer: Decline: bolt torque values for a specific Grove model are in Grove's service manual, not in OSHA text. question: Getting a LICCON error on our Liebherr LTM 1100-5.2, something like 01 0123, and the LMI wont let me telescope. What does that code mean and how do I clear it?
gold_answer: Decline: what a LICCON fault code means and how to clear it is in Liebherr's documentation, not in OSHA rules. question: On a Manitowoc 2250, what's the exact pin pulling order and blocking setup Manitowoc lists for taking the lower boom sections apart?
gold_answer: Decline: the pin-removal order and blocking setup for a Manitowoc 2250 come from Manitowoc's assembly/disassembly procedures. question: potain mdt 389 climbing - how many mast sections can u jack at once and whats the max wind for jacking on that model
gold_answer: Decline: climbing/jacking limits and the jacking wind speed for a Potain MDT 389 are in Potain's manual. 1926.1435 only requires following manufacturer procedures and prohibitions when erecting, climbing and dismantling a tower crane. question: Need the part number for the return hydraulic filter on a National Crane NBT40 and what grade of hydraulic oil they spec. Shop's asking.
gold_answer: Decline: part numbers and fluid specs for a National boom truck are not in OSHA regulations. Nearest is 1926.1412 (inspections and maintenance in general). Tell the user to check the National Crane parts manual or a dealer.

question: Hey so how do you recalibrate the Paltronic on a Palfinger PK 23500 after we swapped a boom cylinder? Like the actual steps.
gold_answer: Decline: the steps to recalibrate Palfinger's Paltronic system are in Palfinger's service documentation. question: What exact rope does Link-Belt call for on the main hoist of a 218 HSL — diameter, construction, part no.? Want to order the right replacement.
gold_answer: Decline: the main-hoist rope spec and part number for a Link-Belt 218 HSL are in the manufacturer's manual. 1926.1414 gives general rope selection and installation criteria and requires following the manufacturer's rope specs, but it does not give model-specific ones. question: How do I set the upper limit switch on a Demag DR-Pro hoist on our bridge crane? Hook comes up way too close to the drum.
gold_answer: Decline: how to adjust the limit switch on a Demag DR-Pro is in the Demag manual. 1910.179 requires an upper limit device on hoists and requires it to be checked, but it gives no adjustment steps for any brand. question: GMK5250L, 120 ft main boom, 80 ft radius, full counterweight, 360 over the side. What's she good for?
gold_answer: Decline: this capacity can only come from the Grove GMK5250L load chart for that exact setup.
